data.name: Gains_Disclaimer
data.value: Figures prepared from your orders, not tax advice. Each sale is matched to the oldest shares bought first (FIFO, Código do IRS art. 43.º). Purchases and sales are in euros at the ECB rate of their own dates; broker and currency conversion fees are expenses. Only sales are taxed: open positions are not declared. Check against the form instructions for the year.

data.name: Gains_EtfCodeNote
data.value: ETFs use code G20 (fund units), whose wording fits best; G90 and G01 are also used, and all three are taxed alike. To confirm.

data.name: Gains_ExclusionNote
data.value: Partial exclusion (Código do IRS art. 43.º n.º 5, since 29 June 2024): 10 % of the gain on listed securities held 2 to 5 years, 20 % for 5 to 8, 30 % from 8. The form asks whether the securities are listed (Sim) and the AT should apply it; the column is informative.

data.name: Gains_InflationNote
data.value: Shares held more than 24 months: the acquisition value is corrected by the inflation coefficient (Código do IRS art. 50.º, for partes sociais). The values here are not corrected: the AT applies the coefficient in the assessment. For ETFs it is not clear that it applies.

data.name: Gains_LinesNote
data.value: One line per sale and purchase it was matched to (FIFO). Tax paid abroad is 0: no tax is withheld on these sales.

data.name: Gains_MissingPurchases
data.value: Some sales are larger than the shares bought before them: the purchase history is incomplete. Import the CSV reports of earlier years.

data.name: Gains_ShortTermHint
data.value: Whether it must be aggregated: see below

data.name: Gains_ShortTermNote
data.value: A positive balance from assets held less than 365 days must be aggregated (englobamento) when your taxable income, including it, reaches the top bracket (83,696 EUR for 2025 income, 86,634 EUR for 2026) — Código do IRS art. 72.º n.º 14. Losses can only be carried forward (5 years) if you aggregate.

data.name: Gains_SplitsHint

data.name: Tax_Disclaimer
data.value: Figures prepared from your data to help fill in the return, not tax advice. Amounts are in euros at the ECB reference rate of the payment date (or the last quote before it, Código do IRS art. 23.º). Dividends use code E11 (no withholding in Portugal) and one line per source country. Check them against the form instructions for the year before submitting.

data.name: Tax_DomesticText
data.value: {0} payments, gross {1}, tax withheld in Portugal {2} ({3}). They are not foreign income, so they are not in Anexo J. A rate of 35 % is the one Portugal applies when the beneficial owner is not identified (omnibus accounts), above the usual 28 %. Declaring them is optional (Anexo E, if you choose to aggregate the income), and how to recover the difference is worth asking a tax adviser.
